question: In round 3 of a ServiceNow Associate ML Engineer Intern interview, the candidate was asked to **design and code in Java a flow where a submitted product review is classified as positive or negative**: positive goes to a thank-you page, negative creates a ticket and redirects. Transformer-based embeddings and other ML models were rejected ('No LLMs'), so a **weighted keyword** solution was expected. The round then moved to **sarcasm handling, JVM internals, memory management, String vs StringBuilder, thread safety, JAR files and Spring Boot**.
lookingFor: Can you design a rule-based solution under constraints without reaching for ML?
Do you write a clean, testable Java implementation with sensible class boundaries?
Do you recognise the limits (negation, sarcasm, mixed sentiment) and propose improvements?
Do you know core Java: String immutability, StringBuilder, memory areas, thread safety?
Can you stay calm and honest when the topic moves outside your experience?
followUps: How would you evaluate this classifier, and which metric matters more: precision or recall on negative reviews?
Why is String immutable in Java, and what are the benefits?
How would you make the classifier thread-safe when weights can be updated at runtime?
When would you finally switch from keywords to a trained model, and how would you prove it is better?
